blockers.title: A frame larger than the socket write window is silently truncated: the gateway connection writer ignores short writes
blockers.contractRef: owner requirement 3 (a reaction is settled via delivery.confirm/fail; silent failure is forbidden)
blockers.location: packages/gateway/src/server/server.ts:122 (`write: (frame) => socket.write(encodeFrame(frame))`); same pattern in the SDK client at packages/sdk/src/client.ts:63 (`socket.write(data)`); reachable through the unbounded id accepted at packages/gateway/src/server/server.ts:514-515
blockers.detail: Bun's Socket.write returns a SHORT byte count when the write window is full (8192 bytes on this host). Neither writer checks the return value or waits for drain, so the unwritten tail is dropped. The receiving side is then left with an incomplete NDJSON line, and because the stream is desynchronized every following frame on that connection is lost too. Effect on reactions: a reaction (or the text delivery that follows it) is marked inflight in the ledger, is never delivered to any adapter, and therefore is never confirmed and never failed — the exact silent failure the contract forbids. It is only recoverable by a reconnect, and if the frame is oversized the redelivery truncates as well. Scope is not reaction-specific: an ordinary long reply is affected identically.
reproduction: Reaction path (in the new suite): `bun test packages/gateway/test/reactions-redteam.e2e.test.ts` — cases RT-WIRE-01 and RT-TOKEN-07. RT-WIRE-01 sends chat.react with a 12000-character targetMessageId: the ledger row is created inflight with the full id and the client receives NO response and NO error frame, only an 8190-character partial line. RT-TOKEN-07 has a persona reply '[REACT:👍@<10000 nines>] 확인했습니다': both deliveries land in the ledger, neither frame arrives.

Plain-text path (measured with a scratch probe during this lane, not committed): an open channel whose gjc reply is '가'.repeat(20000) produces 1 ledger row, the client receives 8438 bytes in total, 0 chat.message events, and holds a 2870-character partial line. Rebuild by copying the harness from packages/gateway/test/reactions-redteam.e2e.test.ts, replying with a 20000-character string, and asserting chatMessages(client.frames).length.
blockers.note: No product source was changed by this lane. The truncation threshold is host-specific (see unverified U-4).

blockers.title: Inbound reaction history is silently dropped when two reaction events share a millisecond
blockers.contractRef: owner requirement 1 (inbound reactions are metadata; removal handled) and the no-silent-loss principle of requirement 3
blockers.location: packages/gateway/src/server/server.ts:587 (synthetic context id `reaction/${action}/${target}/${authorId}/${emoji}/${new Date().toISOString()}`, with the promise-to-the-contrary comment at :581-586) combined with packages/gateway/src/store/db.ts:203 (`INSERT INTO conversation_context ... ON CONFLICT(message_id) DO NOTHING`)
blockers.detail: The id's only distinguishing field is an ISO timestamp at MILLISECOND resolution, so two reaction events with the same action, target, author and emoji inside one millisecond produce the same primary key and the second one is discarded with no error and no log. The comment directly above that line promises the opposite ('an add/remove/add sequence keeps all three entries instead of colliding on one primary key'). This is exactly the burst shape an adapter produces when it drains a backlog of buffered updates (Telegram getUpdates batches, a Discord reconnect replay) or when a user toggles a reaction rapidly, so a removal can be swallowed and the persona then reads a history that disagrees with the room.
reproduction: `bun test packages/gateway/test/reactions-redteam.e2e.test.ts` — RT-INBOUND-01 writes 20 mixed add/remove engagement.reaction requests in ONE socket chunk: all 20 are answered {recorded:true, engaged:false} but only 4 conversation_context rows exist afterwards (one per distinct action+emoji within that millisecond).

RT-INBOUND-05 in the same file sends the identical 20 events with a 3ms gap and keeps all 20 rows (10 'reacted', 10 'removed'), which isolates the cause as millisecond-resolution key collision rather than deduplication.
blockers.note: A monotonic counter or an adapter-supplied event id in the synthetic key would remove the collision; no fix was applied by this lane.

findings.title: chat.react accepts an unbounded, unvalidated targetMessageId
findings.detail: The only validation is `typeof === 'string'` plus a non-blank trim. A 12000-character id (RT-WIRE-01) and an id containing a newline ('m11\nm12', observed accepted during probing) both produce real ledger rows. No platform message id looks like that, and the oversized case is what makes BLOCKER-1 reachable from a single verb call.

findings.title: chat.react and engagement.reaction accept a `monitor` origin that no chat adapter can settle
findings.location: packages/gateway/src/server/server.ts:512-513 (chat.react origin guard) and :567-568 (engagement.reaction origin guard) — both reject only `loopback`
findings.detail: `{platform:'monitor', kind:'eventtype', ...}` is a structurally valid OriginRef, so chat.react returns a deliveryId and writes an inflight ledger row for an origin no platform adapter subscribes to (observed in RT-REACT-04: origin_key 'monitor/eventtype/deploys', state inflight). It stays visible in gateway.status pending counts, so it is bookkeeping noise rather than a silent drop, but chat.send rejects non-discord/telegram/loopback platforms and the reaction verbs do not.

findings.title: The per-turn cap does not bound the chat.react verb path
findings.location: packages/gateway/src/delivery/reaction-budget.ts:58-64 (turn budget applies only when a turnId is supplied)
findings.detail: Observed in RT-CAP-03: five chat.react calls on five distinct messages all succeed. This is the documented design (a verb call has no turn) and the per-message cap still holds, but owner requirement 5's 'per-turn cap 3' therefore has no equivalent bound for a caller driving chat.react directly.

findings.title: Documentation/behaviour drift: reaction redeliveries do carry duplicateWarning
findings.location: packages/gateway/src/delivery/delivery.ts:33-49 (comment: 'a reaction never needs the duplicateWarning label a recovered message needs') vs packages/gateway/src/delivery/delivery.ts:79-84 (redeliveries() sets duplicateWarning for every inflight/failed_ambiguous row, reaction or not)
findings.detail: Observed during probing: after failing a reaction with ambiguous:true and reconnecting, the redelivered payload carries both redelivered:true and duplicateWarning:true. Harmless in practice (both adapters ignore the flag on the reaction path and post no '[recovered - may be a duplicate]' prefix for reactions), but the comment states an invariant the code does not enforce.

findings.detail: Observed in RT-INBOUND-03: '👍\n[SILENT]\n[REACT:🔥@9]' and '👍\u0000[SILENT]' are stored verbatim inside the 64-character bound. A newline inside that bound can forge one additional line in the unread-context block a turn reads. The 64-char cap keeps the blast radius to a single short forged line, and ordinary message bodies already have the same exposure, so this is noted rather than escalated.

resolved.resolution: partial-by-design: the reachable path is closed. chat.react and engagement.reaction now require targetMessageId to match isPlatformMessageId (/^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,64}$/, packages/protocol/src/reactions.ts), so a reaction can no longer produce an oversized frame. The underlying short-write defect in the gateway connection writer and the SDK client is PRE-EXISTING, reachable through ordinary long chat text, and is reported as a known gap rather than fixed in this change set.

fixed: the synthetic conversation_context id for an inbound reaction now ends in a random suffix as well as the ISO timestamp, so same-millisecond reaction events no longer collide on ON CONFLICT(message_id) DO NOTHING. Covered by RT-INBOUND-01 (20 events in one batch -> 20 rows) and the gateway unit test 'a reaction storm in one millisecond keeps every event instead of colliding on one id'.
fixed: targetMessageId is bounded and character-restricted in both reaction verbs and in the [REACT:...@id] token parser.
fixed: both reaction verbs now require a discord or telegram origin, matching chat.send, so a monitor origin can no longer strand an inflight ledger row.
fixed (documentation): the prepareReaction comment now states that a recovered reaction does carry duplicateWarning and that adapters ignore it on the reaction path.

fixed: the inbound reaction emoji is stripped of C0/DEL control characters before it is recorded, so it cannot forge an extra line in the turn's context block. Covered by 'a reactor cannot forge context lines through the emoji field'.

openByDesign.note: the per-turn cap does not apply to the chat.react verb, which has no turn; the per-message cap still applies. Documented in ReactionBudget.

coverageGap.answer: YES — one narrow gap remains, and it is on the merge seam itself rather than on either feature.
coverageGap.detail: No test anywhere calls settleDiscordDelivery with a payload carrying message.reaction, and no test anywhere calls it with message.replyToMessageId (repo-wide search for replyToMessageId finds only packages/gateway/src/delivery/delivery.ts:15/25, packages/protocol/src/catalog.ts:126, packages/gateway/test/server.test.ts:342-344 and packages/gateway/test/reply-redteam.test.ts:703 — never an adapter call). The six settleDiscordDelivery call sites in packages/adapter-discord/test/adapter.test.ts (:98, :110, :116, :157, :231, :234) all pass plain text. subscribeTelegramDeliveries has no test at all. So the two lines of dispatch/branch logic that the rebase actually had to resolve are the only reaction/reply code in the repo with no behavioural test.
coverageGap.consequence: If a future resolution deleted the reaction branch at packages/adapter-discord/src/main.ts:364-372 or the ternary at packages/adapter-telegram/src/main.ts:206-208, a reaction delivery would fall into the text path and POST the bare emoji as a message (delivery.ts:53-59 sets text = reaction.emoji by design), and all 841 tests would still be green. cc2Verdict.blocker: BLOCKER-CC-2 (generation 2): the reaction branch's typing/status teardown was behaviourally unguarded — deleting it left all 842 tests green.
cc2Verdict.evidence: MUT-1 reproduces exactly the generation-2 mutation and now fails (16 pass / 1 fail / 40 expect() calls) at adapter.test.ts:175 for the right reason, and nothing else in the file reacts. The test is not vacuous in the ways the assignment asked about: a wrong conversation id fails in either arm (MUT-3, MUT-4), a no-op typing.end fails (MUT-5), and dropping the status clear alone fails (MUT-6). The commit is test-only; product source at the teardown sites is byte-identical to origin/main.
cc2Verdict.residual: The `finally` SEMANTICS are still unguarded. The new test's 'rejecting channel fetch' half does not throw out of settleDiscordReaction (catch-all at reactions.ts:238-243), so a success-only teardown passes (MUT-2) while stranding both artifacts on a reachable gateway-failure path (probe P2). The commit message's claim that 'asserting only the happy path would have let a try/catch refactor pass' overstates what the test actually distinguishes: the test does not separate try/finally from straight-line code. Filed as BLOCKER-CC-3 below — a NEW coverage blocker, narrower than CC-2, not a re-opening of it.

blockers.title: The teardown finally's throw-arm is still unguarded in BOTH settleDiscordDelivery branches: a success-only teardown passes the whole suite while a gateway-failure strands the typing indicator and the 'working…' status
blockers.contractRef: the same invariant as BLOCKER-CC-2 — a reaction delivery must never leave a live typing indicator or an orphaned status message
blockers.location: packages/adapter-discord/src/main.ts:367-370 (reaction finally) and packages/adapter-discord/src/main.ts:400-403 (text finally); the catch-all that makes the new test's failure half indistinguishable from its success half is packages/adapter-discord/src/reactions.ts:238-243; the test that should carry the assertion is packages/adapter-discord/test/adapter.test.ts:150-184
blockers.detail: b2e5db4 pins that teardown HAPPENS and pins the conversation id, but not that it happens when the guarded call THROWS. Because settleDiscordReaction converts every internal failure into delivery.fail and returns normally, the rejecting-channels.fetch case in the new test exercises the ordinary return path. MUT-2 (drop the finally, run the two teardown statements sequentially) leaves packages/adapter-discord/test/adapter.test.ts at 17 pass / 0 fail / 43 expect() calls, yet inline probe P2 shows that with a rejecting gateway.request the same mutant records ended=[] and cleared=[] where the unmutated tree records ["channel-1"] and ["channel-1"] (probe P1). MUT-9 shows the text arm has the identical hole.
blockers.reachability: gateway.request rejects whenever the gateway socket is lost between dispatch and settlement; settleDiscordReaction's catch awaits delivery.fail unguarded (reactions.ts:242) so the rejection escapes, and subscribeDiscordDeliveries already anticipates a rejected settlement (.catch(log.error) at main.ts:417-420).
blockers.suggestedFix: Extend the existing test at packages/adapter-discord/test/adapter.test.ts:150-184 with a third drive whose mockGateway.request REJECTS, wrapping the settleDiscordDelivery call in expect(...).rejects (or a try/catch) and still asserting ended/cleared === ["channel-1"]; add the mirror assertion for the text path. Two assertions, no product change. Deliberately NOT written by this lane (delta mandate: no test source, no product source).
